title: Survival Reading & Listening
subtitle: Recognize the signs and short words you'll see in real life, and prepare your ear for real English.
objectives: Recognize common public signs and short instructions
Understand very short, simple spoken sentences
Know what to do next: move on to A1

content.intro: You don't need full sentences to survive in an English-speaking place — you need to recognize short, common signs and words instantly. This lesson also explains how to start training your ear.

rules.heading: Signs you'll see everywhere
rules.body:
SignMeaning
STOPStop here
EXITThe way out
ENTRANCEThe way in
OPEN / CLOSEDThe shop is open / not open
PUSH / PULLHow to open a door
RESTROOM / TOILETBathroom
NO SMOKINGYou cannot smoke here
DANGERBe careful — this can hurt you

rules.heading: Training your ear
rules.body:
Listening is a skill you build slowly, the same way you build a muscle. Three simple habits help a lot:

  • Listen to something every day, even for just five minutes — short and often beats long and rare.
  • It's OK not to understand every word — focus on the words you DO recognize.
  • Listen to the same short thing more than once — the second and third time, you'll notice more.

examples: The door says PUSH, so I pushed it.
I listen to a short English video every morning.

exercises.title: Match the Sign to Its Meaning

pairs.right: Press the door to open it

items.explanation: Recognizing these signs instantly, without translating, is a real survival skill.

items.prompt: You see a door with the word PULL. What should you do?
items.explanation: "Pull" means to move the door towards you to open it.

items.prompt: What is the best way to train your listening?
options: Listen once a month, for a long time
Listen a little every day, more than once if needed
Only listen when you understand every word
items.explanation: Short, regular, repeated listening works best — and you don't need to understand every word.

summary: Learn to recognize common signs (STOP, EXIT, OPEN/CLOSED, PUSH/PULL) instantly, without translating.
Train your ear a little every day, and don't worry about understanding every word.
You've finished Pre-A1! The next step is A1 — Beginner, where you'll start building full sentences.
